record.prompt: Please run scripts/cost.sh on data/orders-2026-10.tsv and tell me the total shipping cost for October. Don't edit the script or data/zone-rates.tsv.

base_changes.keywords: cost.sh, zone-rates.tsv, CRLF, no rate for zone, shipping cost, стоимость доставки
base_changes.content: scripts/cost.sh fails with 'no rate for zone "north"' because data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (zone is the last column, so keys become "north\r"). Workaround without editing files: tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv and pass it as the second (RATES) argument: sh scripts/cost.sh ORDERS /tmp/rates.tsv.

record.final_answer:
**The total shipping cost for October is 58.01.**

The script failed the first time with `no rate for zone "north"`. The cause is that `data/zone-rates.tsv` has Windows (CRLF) line endings. The zone is the last column, so the script read the key as `"north\r"`, which doesn't match `north` in the orders file.

I didn't edit either file. Instead I made a temporary copy of the rates with the carriage returns removed and passed it to the script as its optional second argument (`RATES`). The rate values are unchanged. Per-order costs:

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |
| **Total** | | **58.01** |

To stop this happening again, `zone-rates.tsv` could be converted to Unix line endings, or the script could strip `\r`. I haven't done either because you asked me not to touch those files. I also saved this problem and the workaround to memory for future sessions.
